headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared files and permissive tool paths; Continue can write workspace files while ChatGPT Desktop reads files and app context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can write to workspace files and use MCP, while ChatGPT Desktop reads filesystem content and app context from files/screenshots. That creates a plausible file-based injection path if Continue outputs attacker-controlled instructions into shared files that ChatGPT then ingests. The bridge is not fully documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Continue writes instruction-like content into a file ChatGPT Desktop reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files in ChatGPT Desktop
Require human review before copying agent output into files
Restrict Continue to non-prompt files only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code while Continue reads workspace files and open buffers. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or uploaded content can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs. Continue’s broad network egress increases exposure, but the exact transfer path is not fully documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file tree
IF sensitive files are present in that shared workspace
mitigations: Keep separate repositories or folders per agent
Remove secrets and sensitive files from shared workspaces
Turn off file upload/attachment workflows for ChatGPT Desktop when unnecessary
Limit Continue to a sanitized subset of files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write access and shared state via filesystem, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context but cannot write the filesystem. They can still conflict over the same mutable workspace if Continue edits files that ChatGPT later consumes, causing racey or inconsistent state. The asymmetry lowers this from high because only one agent writes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or project
IF Continue writes files while ChatGPT Desktop reads those files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working copy
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches or snapshots for handoff
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool workflows and ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived outputs; if one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. Because Continue requires user approval for tool calls and ChatGPT Desktop is vendor-mediated, the chain is not fully automatic, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop output is pasted or saved into Continue as authoritative input
IF Continue then uses that output to generate code or tool calls without verification
mitigations: Add a human verification step between agents
Require source citations before acting on generated facts
Use a checklist to compare outputs against original files
Limit tool execution to reviewed diffs only
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Continue handles workspace files and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is justified from the broader data-handling surface overlap. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent without a matching policy
IF the chosen model provider or storage region conflicts with organizational requirements
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Confirm vendor retention settings before use
Store API keys only in approved secret managers
Document which data classes each agent may process
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and DPA review
